reading.text:
UNIT def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.Ito.simpleIntegral -- reading (locked before any Lean)

Paper notion: the Ito integral of a simple predictable process,
  int_0^t phi dW = sum_{i<N} xi_i (W_{t_{i+1} ∧ t} - W_{t_i ∧ t})
(textbook; the base of the L^2 construction behind sec. 3/4). Faithful Lean: exactly this sum,
pathwise (as a function of omega), with the truncation at t (so that the integral up to t is
correct for t inside an interval), using the Brownian path W of the integral's driver.
Harmless: defining it only at the terminal time if the integral up to t is taken by
multiplying the integrand by 1_{[0,t]} elsewhere. Not faithful: the increment W_{t_{i+1}} - W_{t_i}
paired with xi_{i+1} (forward-looking), missing truncation when the integral is used at
intermediate times, or increments of the wrong process.

Paper context (sec. 2, sec. 3, sec. 4, App. A). Standing basis: (Omega,F,(F_t),P) satisfying the usual
conditions, horizon T>0, d-dimensional Brownian motion W and an independent Poisson random
measure N on R_+ x E with intensity dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a countably generated (E,E);
(F_t) is the usual augmentation of the filtration generated by W, N and an independent initial
sigma-field F_0. Stochastic integrals int Z dW (Z in H^2_W: R^{m x d}-valued predictable,
E int_0^T |Z|_F^2 dt < oo) and int int U dNtilde (U in H^2_N) are the L^2 (Ito /
compensated-Poisson isometry) integrals; they are true L^2 martingales, cadlag, and are used in
identities holding a.s. for every t (sec. 3, "solution"). The paper never constructs these
integrals itself: it takes the standard construction (Applebaum sec. 4, He-Wang-Yan). So every
unit below is infrastructure: the paper's notion is the textbook one, and a faithful Lean
definition is one that (together with the other definitions) yields the textbook object on the
paper's basis for every integrand the paper's claims use; junk values outside that class are
harmless only if every proposition restricts to the class.

comparison.text:
Comparison: def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.Ito.simpleIntegral (ItoSimpleIntegrand.lean:54-62)

Reading: int_0^t phi dW = sum_{i<N} xi_i (W_{t_{i+1} ∧ t} - W_{t_i ∧ t}), pathwise, with
truncation at t, increments of the integral's Brownian path, coefficient xi_i paired with the
increment over its own interval.
Lean: simpleIntegral W H t omega = sum_{i : Fin H.N} H.xi i omega * (W.W (min (partition i.succ) t)
omega - W.W (min (partition i.castSucc) t) omega). Exactly the formula, pathwise, truncated at t
(min with t), xi_i paired with (t_i, t_{i+1}] (no forward-looking pairing), W the Brownian motion
passed in. At t <= 0 every term is xi_i (W_t - W_t) = 0 (simpleIntegral_zero for t = 0).
Verdict: faithful.
